subject: Private deployment interconnect patterns & ingress hardening

Subject: Private deployment interconnect patterns & ingress hardening

Hi Tim / Acme ops team —

Thanks again for taking the time to move the private deployment evaluation forward. Attached are the reference artifacts we mentioned in the kickoff: vpc-interconnect-diagram.vsdx (high-level control/data plane flows) and ingress-policy.yaml (draft ingress L7 rules and allowed CIDR lists).

Request: could your network team review the diagram and ingress policy with a focus on the following items and share any constraints or preferences by EOD Monday?
- Preferred interconnect (IPsec VPN, managed transit, or direct MPLS) and any AWS/GCP/Azure specific constructs you need us to support.
- Ingress termination expectations (do you want L4 pass-through to customer LB, or would you prefer Redwood terminate TLS at our edge and forward to customer private endpoints?)
- Egress controls and audit/logging: what level of egress filtering + TLS inspection is required for your compliance teams?

We'd also appreciate if the team can flag required ASN ranges, IP pools for NAT, and any latency/SLA targets that will affect routing choices.

Internal: Irene/Kim/Logan — please weigh in on operational requirements (BFD, BGP timers, NAT pools, monitoring hooks) and point to any runbook artifacts we should include in our handoff.

Next steps: if we have answers to the bullets above, I’ll produce a final architecture readout and proposed cutover plan.

Thanks,

Stephanie Nguyen
Head of Private Deployments, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Private deployment interconnect patterns & ingress hardening

Stephanie —

Thanks for the diagram and the policy. Quick notes from an initial pass (we'll have a formal readout Monday after we sync with our network architects):

- Interconnect: Acme prefers a private L3 transit over a managed cloud interconnect (MPLS/Direct Connect equivalent) for production traffic. We do keep a VPN fallback for DR.
- BGP: we'll push BGP session limits to avoid high session churn; prefer eBGP multihop with a /30 peer addressing plan.
- Ingress TLS: for our use case we prefer TLS be terminated at Acme's LB inside our VPCs (no external TLS termination) due to internal mTLS and certificate management. If Redwood needs to inspect traffic for telemetry, we can provision a mirror TAP/collector (no inline TLS termination).
- Egress: SOC team requires flow logs + ability to export to our SIEM (S3 + Kinesis/Datadog). Any TLS inspection must be explicit and agreed — we prefer metadata-only export initially.

Attached a markup (acme-markup-comments.pdf) with redlines on the diagram and some suggested CIDR allocations.

Tim
Tim Barker
EdgeWorks — Senior Network Architect

Looping in ops concerns from the platform side —

From an operational/runbook perspective we need the following before we can approve a final design:
- NAT and IP management: explicit NAT pools + documentation of which services use SNAT vs DNAT. We should reserve a /24 for Redwood-managed NAT (documented in the runbook).
- BFD: recommended for fast failover; please confirm vendor support on the customer’s side (Tim, is BFD supported end-to-end?).
- Probe & monitoring hooks: we need an HTTP healthcheck path and an optional TCP probe for LB backends. We'll expose metrics via Prometheus pushgateway; Acme should provide a read-only Prometheus endpoint or replicate metrics to our telemetry pipeline.
- Cutover runbook: cold path and warm path, rollback triggers, escalations, and contact list. I attached a template (runbook-template.md) — please fill the sections about IP allocations and expected maintenance windows.

I'll sync offline with Logan on IPAM and with Irene on certificate rotation.

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Platform Operations, Redwood Inference

Team / Acme —

I did a technical pass on the diagram and ingress policy. Key items to address before we finalize the control/data plane split:

1) Control plane topology
- Control plane (management/control messages) must be encrypted and authenticated via mutual TLS to Acme’s control-plane endpoint. No control plane traffic should transit the customer data plane.
- Control plane heartbeat and telemetry should be on a separate routing domain (we suggest ASN 64510 for our control-plane peering).

2) Data plane forwarding
- Data plane will honor Acme’s CIDR map; we should implement prefix-lists to avoid accidental advertisement of internal ranges.
- For high-throughput customers, enable continuous batching on the local inference nodes and ensure MTU is consistent across the interconnect to avoid fragmentation.

3) Egress & audit
- Redwood will support flow logs export to Acme S3/Kinesis. For now we will not perform TLS termination — matching Tim's ask. If Acme later approves telemetry mirroring, we'll document the collector interfaces.

4) Ports and firewall rules (suggested minimal set)
- Control plane mTLS: TCP 443 (mutual TLS)
- BGP: TCP 179 with eBGP multihop as needed
- Health checks: TCP 8080/HTTP health path
- Prometheus scrape (optional): TCP 9090 read-only

5) Certificate rotation
- Use ACME/automated rotation for node certificates; control-plane certs rotate on a 60-day cadence with a 10-day overlap renewal window. Add a checklist to the runbook so ops can validate rotation during cutover.

I attached an annotated diagram with suggested tag changes (annotated-diagram.png). Implementation notes: Logan, we'll need the IPAM csv early so I can populate prefix-lists and BGP neighbor configs.

Irene
Irene Choi
Principal Engineer, Private Deployments, Redwood Inference
